The *Śrīgurustutiratnāvalī* composed by Śrī Govindakaula.
Homage to the Goddess Śrī!
Oṃ, salutation to the glorious Guru, who is Śiva.
Salutation to the illustrious Gaṇapati.
May there be prosperity!
Having directly realized his own stainless nature, which consists of the imperishable,
and having abandoned the deluded mind, he who is praised as "Maheśa" by gods, sages, and mortals;
With his compassionate gaze, he instantly liberates the bound devotees;
[he is] Kauleśa, Kula, the excellent Guru, Vāgme, the Lord, and the Sovereign (Sāhib). || 1 ||
Oh, how wonderful! From the mere manifestation of that one Sovereign, the universe arises;
through His glance, it pervades all existence for a moment, and then, as if at the close of a breath, it vanishes back into dissolution.

I bow to that auspicious Śiva, the Sovereign Lord, who is autonomous, eternally risen, all-pervading, full, and ever-pure; he is the inexhaustible treasure of bliss, the jewel of consciousness and sound.

He who, from his foundational lotus in the beginning, illuminates every world with his splendors, and having assumed an immortal form, dwells within the source of the abundant lotuses, pouring forth [nectar] from his lotus feet.

I worship that Śambhu, known by the name Sāhib, who shines as the supreme hand within the treasury of the universe, sprinkling the gods, sages, ancestors, artisans, and assemblies of pilgrims with showers of nectar.
The Creator, through the taste of worshipping whose lotus feet, transcends the hundreds of creations.

O Lord, Viṣṇu, the friend of the Victorious One (Jiṣṇu), protects the three worlds through the worship of Your lotus feet; Rudra, Īśa, and Sadāśiva [protect them] through the withdrawal [of the world]; and You Yourself, O Master, whose delight is in sovereignty and whose very self is dependent upon the community of devotees, maintain the maintenance, destruction, and concealment of the triple world by the mere knitting of Your eyebrows.
You are the refuge of all, the source of reality and prosperity; yet in truth, You are Yourself without support.
You are the all-knowing one, the possessor of the parts such as the creator-ship, and you are concealed within your mantle.
You are a treasure-house of compassion, you are the supreme greatness; O Śrī Sahiba, I praise You.
The body is called "body" because it is imagined; O Hṛṣīkeśa, go to the assembly that is like a heap of stones.
Even powerful beings rejoice clearly in order to bring about the presence of the states of existence within the cycle of rebirth.
I bow to that Śiva, the life of all living beings, by whose ray of light the vital breath draws breath.
I take refuge in the Lord Sahib, my own innate Cinnātha, the supreme Guru and the ultimate abode.
And he who constantly awakens the multitude of all beings sleeping in the illusion of Māyā.
He who is himself changeless undergoes the transformation of the six states of being.
In one or many ways, sport with Your own multitude of waves of power.
O Lord, I meditate upon You, who are inferred from Your own manifestations, and who are not perceived as having a single form alone.
In the system of logic, the agent is the liberated person; in Sāṅkhya, it is the Puruṣa; and in the Buddhist tradition, it is the Jina.
In the teaching of sound, it is the essence of speech; in the path of ritual action, it belongs to the lineage of Gaṇeśa.
Brahmā alone is at the pinnacle of the Vedas; he is this Hari who is indeed celebrated in the Vaiṣṇava scriptures.
In the Śaiva tradition, I take refuge in that Lord Śambhu, who is peerless and entirely stainless. || 8 ||
This eternal, blissful, and stainless one laughs at the bathing places of the worldly paths.

I remember the Lord Sahib, who is free from duality, whose creative reckoning is without beginning or end, who is non-dual and consists of pure consciousness; who is a vibration without movement, joined with the unsurpassed digit, the Guru, the stainless, the sovereign refuge of all, the incomparable and eternal. 9. Sa.
Thus I dwell, illuminating all around in heaven with a body of discernment and joy.
By whom, in the past, that splendor filled with the awakening to truth was made to shine forth in heaven.

I praise my own Guru, Sāhib, who is compassionate, auspicious, and possesses a fresh body; he is self-luminous, pure, and beautiful by nature, and he has sent forth his dear disciples upon the earth. 10.
In that abode, she whose form is Bhairava should be fully meditated upon by the great-souled ones within the thousand-petaled lotus.
Upon a lotus at her head is the white vowel [Ā], she has three eyes, sits upon the moon, and possesses the luster of the moon.
The left hand holds a book marked with the moon, and the goddess is embraced by [the deity].
I meditate upon that Supreme Śiva, the Sovereign, who is solely intent on bestowing grace upon his devotees. || 11 ||
The serpent Antavāyana and Bhujoka were on the earth, while Śaśin was on his forehead and Īkṣaṇa was upon the ground.
Thus, this very Śaṅkaranātha, while wandering, remains embodied as the Ācārya.
He directly bestows grace through the vision of supreme non-duality and by means of speech that grants liberation.
I bow to you, that auspicious Lord Śiva, who is the dense mass of consciousness and bliss, and who is sovereign. 12.
Those who are delighted by the streams of supreme nectar flowing from the two feet of Rādhikā.
Having crossed over the two [worlds] by means of Your own light, You incessantly satisfy Your lotus feet for the sake of those who have sought refuge as Your servants.
I remember that Lord Sāhiba, the Supreme Śiva, who bestows sovereignty upon His own realm, who is eternally joyful, and who is adorned with the title "Vanditakta" (the Adored). 13.
The soul of the savior, the deliverer from existence, joined by the immortals, the world-protectors, and the lords of the senses.
He is the ocean of the nectar of all speech, filled with the joy of consciousness, and eternal.
Though greater than the cosmic egg, yet subtler than the subtlest atom; light beyond darkness, the light of all lights.
Through the discernment of my own self, I perceive that Supreme Śiva; I worship that Sovereign Lord. || 14 ||
Since speech [proceeds] from the Lord of the Mandākinī, who is skilled in destroying the suffering of those who bow before him;
According to the opinion of the sages, [patience] is the purification of mental turbidity, straightforwardness, forbearance, pure, and the locus of serenity.
The expansion of the stream, which has descended into the body, is honored at the sacred bathing places (*tīrtha*).
I salute the Lord of the Universe, the best of teachers, the benefactor Śiva, the all-pervading Sahib. || 15 ||
This Māyā is the honored primordial woman, whose festival is the play of absolute freedom.
She bestows the manifestation of duality through the veil of the existence and non-existence of her own natural states.
By whom are the states of the enjoyer and the enjoyed separated, and by whom are those deluded ones bound?
I take refuge in that Guru, the Lord, who is the master of the three worlds and whose nature is easy to awaken. 16.
The fortune of that Lord of the World, whose mind is ever-attached to his lotus feet—
Having abandoned even the artificiality of the created, it has taken firm refuge in the joy of the uncreated.
The all-pervading Lord, whose full power is manifested through liberation divided by the throbbing enjoyment.
I bow to Śrīnātha, the sovereign of the circle of gurus, the Lord, the Sahib. || 17 ||
Let there be space; the moon shines forth clearly, and it is enjoyed when it is gentle.
And Sarvaddhi, Janārdana, and Caṇḍānalaujas were stationed by the hosts of gods.
Even in the three worlds, O Moon rich in digits, that peerless Lord is beautiful and worthy of worship.
O Maheśa, I incessantly praise You, the Sovereign Lord who is the refuge for those who worship; You are Śambhu, possessed of supreme power, the singular consumer of all afflictions.
You are the one who causes the world's dissolution; you are free from wretchedness even in the depths of misery; you are the Great Time, the time of all times.
I worship you, Śrī Sāhib, the Great Lord and Guru who transcends all—the one whose nature is indivisible, who is Indra, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Madhuripu, and the Lotus-born Brahmā. 19.
The moon and sun are in the *kṣaṇa* [position], the eight powers, Giriśa, and the head of the sky are in the navel and the void.
The ocean dwelling within his belly, whose mouth is fire, and who is illuminated by subtle nectar.
O you who are the ear of the quarters, the ground for the feet, the very life-breath of the world, and whose nature is indeed not cruel!
I meditate upon you, Śrīnātha, the most illustrious king, whose form is wondrous, the Sovereign Lord.
Śaṅkara’s face is as vast as the sky, eternally praised by the gods.
The illustrious Lord of Kuṇṭha and Pinākin is indeed the essence of nectar and joy for all.
I bow to Śiva, the supreme teacher of the world, who resembles the fire at the end of an aeon and resides within the heart.
I bow to the all-pervading Lord Sāhib, who has traversed the unsurpassed peace, who is eternal, unborn, and sovereign. || 21 ||
The illustrious Viśveśvara Bhairava, exceedingly compassionate, is united with Harṣeśvarī.
He also accepted as his disciples those who were jewels of the traditional lineage and the oral transmission, and who had taken refuge in him.
Though unmanifest, he is the stainless incarnation of compassion, the very ocean of awakening.
May that Sāhiba, the lord of the Kaula, who possesses vast fame, be victorious.
He who is the form of emptiness, yet inlaid with full power; the abode of the void, rich in nectar and bliss; who nourishes the entire world; the source of qualities, yet partless.
Even though he is the locus of the digits of both duality and non-duality, he is praised by the sages, the lords of yogis.
I take refuge in that Lord, the Supreme Śiva, who is the very nature of consciousness, abundant, and the Guru. || 23 ||
I remain here with joy, my mouth resting upon Sarasvatī, the tradition of Brahman.
He himself was accompanied by Drāksaṅkarṣaṇa, Caivata, Agramahāsena, and others.
O Guru, the world constantly praises Śrīnātha, who is invincible and supreme.
I bow to the Supreme Śiva, the venerable Sāhib, who abides in form and is the life-force of all. || 24 ||
O Blessed One, God of gods, Lord, whose nature consists of mantra, the practitioner of mantra, and the object of mantra!
O Śrī Śrī Kaula, O Kuleśa, O Teacher, O Parānandādinātha, grant fearlessness!
With his body embraced by Śakti, his face serene, he granted the desired boon.
May you always attain the supreme sandals of Śiva and Śivā, along with progeny, through this prostration. || 25 ||

I praise you, O Śrī Sāhiba, the true Guru, who holds the three abodes, who is the sun that dispels the darkness of duality, and who is the ocean of nectar-rays of compassion, whose heart is a blue lotus, and who is the fire that consumes the bonds of worldly existence.

Victorious is the auspicious Śrīpādukā, the sovereign of the three worlds, whose worshipable feet protect from evil, whose remembrance destroys great sins, and which grants the fulfillment of desires.
He who possesses the power and majesty of the three gods, yet is radiant like the crescent of the moon.
Having willed the cessation of the flood [of mental constructs], he abides within the limit of space as the great pervader.
He is the reality of consciousness, whose power is unfailing and pervasive; he is the one who has arisen as the transmental (unmanā) and the sentient.
I worship you, the Supreme Śiva, the Sovereign praised by those who know the truth. || 27 ||
O All-pervading Lord, what indeed is Your meditation upon forms such as time, shape, and direction, which have no physical body?
You are the one who has manifested the purpose of the entire universe; O Janaka, how could there be a ritual of worship for you?
O Lord, what praise can there be for Your body, which shines with the golden splendor of the letters from 'A' to 'Kṣa'?
I take refuge in you, the Lord—the Truth, the Peaceful, the Unsurpassed, and the Best of Gurus. || 28 ||
Having first bathed in the Bindu-saras with the thick nectar of the moon, becoming completely purified;
Having sprinkled the supporting ground with natural flowers illuminated by the fourth [state] of consciousness, O Jālandhara...
Having always made Nanda’s head a vessel for the priceless offering of water, his heart being full.
O Lord of the body, I worship you, the Sahib, together with the Goddess in this abode of the body. || 27 ||
O enemy-subduer, how many fools in this world claim to be friends?
The ocean drenches the mountains; indeed, the end-maker approaches as the world bows down.
Worldly enjoyment is considered a stain, whereas the festival of worshipping Your sandals is considered a virtuous deed.
I praise you, that compassionate Śrī Sāhiba Śaṅkara, whose feet I have approached.
By good fortune, O Śrī Maheśvara, whose nature is that of Maheśa, O Lord of the illustrious and powerful teachers, this *Stotraratnāvalī* consisting of thirty jewels of the heart,
strung together with gems, is offered with devotion at the lotus feet of the Lord renowned as the venerable Śrī Kauleśvara Sāhiba, for the sake of his satisfaction through light. 31.
The omnipresent Lord, having obtained grace through worship of the lotus feet of this Protector, [bestows his favor].
O you whose nature is consciousness, honored by the virtuous, you who are called the light that illuminates all.
Salutations to the illustrious Goddess;
may this one, whose lotus feet are praised by the lords of serpents, the guardians of the quarters, and the lords of the mountains, [protect us].
Victorious is the one whose very self is Śarva, who has illuminated the state of being a great devotee of Maheśvara.
In the illustrious Śaka year numbered by the Vedas (4), the oceans (4), the logic-systems (6), and the moon (1), of this Lord of the Universe...
He, a bee at the lotus-feet [of the Lord], was present during the festival on the eighth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Madhu.
Śrī Govinda offers this series of nine jewels to you every day.
Those wise ones who recite this even on their own throats shall attain the glory of both worldly enjoyment and liberation. 33.

Thus ends the *Śrīgurustutiratnāvalī*, composed by Śrī Govindakaula, who is a follower of the lotus feet of the venerable Śrī Jyotiṣprakāśaka Kaulānanda, the great teacher of Maheśvara. May there be well-being!
In the year 39, on the tenth day of the month of Vaiśākha, this [work] was painted by those who know what is to be known.
Salutation to the illustrious Goddess, the bestower of spiritual accomplishments.
Salutations to the venerable Guru, who is Śiva.
Salutations to the illustrious Gaṇapati.
Oṃ. Having seen the God of gods, Mahādeva, the Lord who bears the trident, with a gracious countenance, Pārvatī prostrated herself and then rose up.
With palms joined in reverence and her head bowed in humility,
the Goddess spoke these humble words with a smile to the Supreme Lord.
The Goddess said:
O Blessed One, O Supreme Lord, you who are affectionate toward those who have come for refuge;
by your grace, I have heard the entire supreme *Ḍāmara*.
The essence of the tantras from beginning to end is found in detail within the *Yāmala* and other such works.
Now, O Blessed One, I wish to hear about the divine worship of the nine Durgās as proclaimed by you, which is concealed within all the tantras.
The excellent skull of a Kāśyapa bestows all desires upon practitioners.
Śrī Bhairava.
O Goddess, this most secret [teaching] has not been told by me to anyone.
This worship yields the fruit of ten million offerings of the Samaya-initiation.
This most secret of secrets, which was to be concealed, has been kept for a long time.
Now I shall speak to you; I will explain it in great detail.
It must be guarded with effort and protected like one's own son.
Listen with a single-minded heart and full devotion, O Pārvatī; there exist various kinds of mantras, including their seed-syllables (bījas), as taught in the Āgamas.
Various tantras are collected here, O Maheśvarī. 9.
In the Kali age, those mantras have become partless (niṣkala) and devoid of potency,
because of substances lacking the purity of women and because of the impurity of the ground.
From falsehood, from envy, from deceit, from maliciousness, and from greed for wealth.
O lady of excellent hips, all [rites] that have become fruitless are perfected.
The treatise on truth and scripture, as well as the proposition and the established conclusion, are indeed accomplished.
That [teaching] is corrupted by disrespect and likewise by a lack of devotion to the guru; however, within it, there exists that which is the essential core, which bestows manifest results.
And the Rudrayāmala Tantra, which consists of sixty-four [parts], is supreme.
It is joined with various auspicious mantras and the worship of the samayas.
Without the initiations of the pledges and so forth, even initiation by means of mantras is fruitless.
For Śivā is indeed Brahmā, she is indeed Viṣṇu, she is indeed Śiva, and she is indeed Mṛtyu. || 15 ||
O Goddess, O Rārohe, the daily worship, recitation, and other rites always attain success.
O Goddess, sacrifices such as the Homa and others, or worship at the proper time, are [ineffective] without the worship of the Samaya.
